escape.simple: to get away from danger or a bad situation
escape.natural: He stayed calm and looked for a way to escape the fire.
escape.positive: Escaping a bad habit is the first step towards a better life.
escape.leadership: The leader checked every exit and helped the team escape safely.
escape.factual: The prisoners escaped through a tunnel dug over three months.
escape.general: The cat escaped through the open window before anyone noticed.

gun.natural: He saw the gun and raised his hands slowly.
gun.positive: A gun in trained hands protects the innocent.
gun.leadership: The officer kept the gun secured and briefed the squad on safety.
gun.factual: A service rifle is checked and cleared before it is handed over.
gun.general: The guard carried his gun on his shoulder through the night.

award.simple: a prize given for good work
award.natural: He felt proud when his name was called for the award.
award.positive: An award reminds us that sincere effort is noticed.
award.leadership: The team leader shared the award credit with every member.
award.factual: The award is given every year to the best cadet in the academy.
award.general: She kept the award on the shelf beside her books.

guts.natural: It took guts to admit the mistake in front of everyone.
guts.positive: Guts grow stronger each time you choose the right path under pressure.
guts.leadership: A leader shows guts by taking responsibility when the plan fails.
guts.factual: The word guts is used informally for courage and determination.
guts.general: He had the guts to speak first in the meeting.

god.natural: He closed his eyes and thanked God for his family.
god.positive: Faith in God gives many people calm and strength.
god.leadership: A good leader respects the faith of every person in the team.
god.factual: India recognises many faiths and protects the freedom to worship.
god.general: She visits the temple every Sunday to pray to God.

fight.natural: He decided to fight the problem instead of running from it.
fight.positive: We can fight any difficulty with patience and a clear plan.
fight.leadership: The leader taught the team to fight fear, not each other.
fight.factual: Soldiers train daily so they can fight effectively when called.
fight.general: The children fought over the last seat in the bus.

achieve.simple: to reach a goal by effort
achieve.natural: He wrote the target down so he could achieve it.
achieve.positive: Small daily steps help you achieve big results.
achieve.leadership: A leader helps every member achieve more than they thought possible.
achieve.factual: The unit achieved its training target two weeks ahead of schedule.
achieve.general: You can achieve good marks with steady revision.

fake.natural: He noticed the signature looked fake and asked for proof.
fake.positive: Rejecting fake shortcuts builds real confidence.
fake.leadership: The leader checked the documents so no fake claim entered the file.
fake.factual: Fake news spreads fastest when people share without checking.
fake.general: The watch was fake, but it still kept good time.

hard work.simple: steady effort over a long time
hard work.natural: He believed hard work would take him further than luck.
hard work.positive: Hard work turns ordinary ability into real achievement.
hard work.leadership: The leader worked harder than anyone and set the standard.
hard work.factual: Consistent hard work improves skill more than short bursts of effort.
hard work.general: Hard work in the morning leaves the evening free.

imagination.simple: the ability to form new ideas in the mind
imagination.natural: His imagination turned a simple box into a spaceship.
imagination.positive: Imagination lets us see solutions that do not exist yet.
imagination.leadership: A leader uses imagination to plan for problems before they arrive.
imagination.factual: Imagination helps children learn language faster.
imagination.general: She has a lively imagination and writes stories at night.

aim.simple: a goal you want to reach
aim.natural: He fixed his aim on the target and breathed out.
aim.positive: A clear aim keeps the mind focused under pressure.
aim.leadership: The leader explained the aim before dividing the tasks.
aim.factual: The aim of the exercise was to test teamwork under fatigue.
aim.general: My aim this year is to read twelve books.

kill.natural: He could not kill even an insect without reason.
kill.positive: Choose to kill bad habits before they grow.
kill.leadership: The leader ordered the team to kill the rumour with facts.
kill.factual: The pest control team had to kill the infected crop to save the field.
kill.general: The frost killed the young plants overnight.

lose.simple: to fail to win, or to no longer have something
lose.natural: He accepted that he might lose, but he would not quit.
lose.positive: You lose a match, not the lesson it teaches.
lose.leadership: A leader absorbs the blame when the team loses.
lose.factual: The team lost the final by three points.
lose.general: Be careful not to lose your keys again.

aloof.natural: He seemed aloof, so nobody asked him for help.
aloof.positive: Being quiet is fine, but staying aloof weakens a team.
aloof.leadership: A leader cannot afford to stay aloof from the people he leads.
aloof.factual: The word aloof describes someone who keeps a distance.
aloof.general: The new boy was aloof for a week, then joined the games.

bribe.simple: money given to get an unfair favour
bribe.natural: He refused the bribe and reported it to his senior.
bribe.positive: Refusing a bribe protects your self-respect more than money can.
bribe.leadership: A leader sets the example by rejecting every bribe openly.
bribe.factual: Taking a bribe is a criminal offence under the Prevention of Corruption Act.
bribe.general: The clerk was arrested for accepting a bribe.

jungle.natural: They lost the path in the jungle and waited for daylight.
jungle.positive: The jungle teaches patience, alertness and respect for nature.
jungle.leadership: The leader kept the group together in the jungle.
jungle.factual: Jungles hold more than half of the world's plant and animal species.
jungle.general: We saw deer and peacocks in the jungle.

identity.natural: He was proud of his identity and his roots.
identity.positive: A strong identity helps you stay steady under pressure.
identity.leadership: A leader respects every identity in a mixed team.
identity.factual: Aadhaar is used as proof of identity in India.
identity.general: The wallet held his identity card and licence.

books.simple: printed or written works you read
books.natural: He opened a book whenever he felt restless.
books.positive: Books give knowledge and calm in equal measure.
books.leadership: A leader reads widely to make better decisions.
books.factual: The library holds over ten thousand books.
books.general: She keeps her books neatly on the shelf.

money.simple: coins and notes used to buy things
money.natural: He saved money every month instead of spending it.
money.positive: Money managed well brings security, not show.
money.leadership: A leader spends team money as carefully as his own.
money.factual: The rupee is issued by the Reserve Bank of India.
money.general: He forgot his money at home and paid by phone.

riot.natural: The shopkeeper closed early when the riot began.
riot.positive: A calm word can stop a crowd before a riot starts.
riot.leadership: The officer controlled the riot without firing a shot.
riot.factual: Riot control units use shields, helmets and water cannon.
riot.general: The market stayed shut after the riot.

mother.natural: He called his mother first whenever something good happened.
mother.positive: A mother's patience shapes a child's character.
mother.leadership: A leader cares for his team the way a mother cares for her family.
mother.factual: Motherhood is protected by law in most countries.
mother.general: My mother makes the best tea in the house.

praise.natural: He felt shy when his teacher praised him.
praise.positive: Honest praise costs nothing and lifts a whole team.
praise.leadership: A leader praises in public and corrects in private.
praise.factual: The report praised the unit for its quick response.
praise.general: She praised the food and asked for the recipe.

organise.natural: He organised his notes the night before the exam.
organise.positive: Organising small tasks early removes half the stress.
organise.leadership: The leader organised the camp so everyone had a clear job.
organise.factual: The event was organised by the student council.
organise.general: Please organise these files by date.

bright.natural: The bright light made him shade his eyes.
bright.positive: A bright mind and a steady heart make a strong officer.
bright.leadership: The leader saw a bright solution where others saw a dead end.
bright.factual: The brightest star in the night sky is Sirius.
bright.general: She wore a bright yellow dress to the function.

plan.simple: a set of steps to reach a goal
plan.natural: He made a plan before touching the problem.
plan.positive: A simple plan followed well beats a clever plan abandoned.
plan.leadership: The leader made a plan, shared it and kept it flexible.
plan.factual: The operation followed a plan rehearsed three times.
plan.general: Our plan for Sunday is a long walk by the river.

meet.natural: He was glad to meet his old friend at the station.
meet.positive: Every meeting is a chance to learn something new.
meet.leadership: The leader meets the team every morning for five minutes.
meet.factual: The two officers met at the border post to discuss the handover.
meet.general: Let us meet outside the theatre at six.

lonely.natural: He felt lonely on the first night away from home.
lonely.positive: Loneliness can be used to think and grow.
lonely.leadership: A leader notices the lonely member and brings him into the group.
lonely.factual: Loneliness is common among people who live far from family.
lonely.general: The old house felt lonely after the children moved out.

border.natural: The soldier kept watch at the border through the night.
border.positive: A calm border lets trade and friendship grow.
border.leadership: The leader checked the border post and spoke to every guard.
border.factual: India shares borders with seven countries.
border.general: We stopped at a small town on the border.

honest.natural: He was honest even when the truth cost him.
honest.positive: Honesty builds trust that no cleverness can replace.
honest.leadership: A leader must be honest about bad news first.
honest.factual: The officer was praised for his honest report.
honest.general: Be honest with me about what happened.

blunder.natural: He realised his blunder and corrected it at once.
blunder.positive: A blunder admitted early becomes a lesson, not a habit.
blunder.leadership: The leader owned the blunder instead of blaming the team.
blunder.factual: The filing blunder delayed the application by a week.
blunder.general: I made a blunder by calling her by the wrong name.

air force.simple: the branch of the armed forces that fights in the sky
air force.natural: He dreamed of joining the Air Force as a pilot.
air force.positive: The Air Force guards the sky so the ground can live in peace.
air force.leadership: The Air Force captain briefed the crew before the sortie.
air force.factual: The Indian Air Force was founded in 1932.
air force.general: The Air Force display drew thousands of visitors.

progress.natural: He measured his progress each week to stay motivated.
progress.positive: Slow progress is still progress worth protecting.
progress.leadership: The leader tracked progress without pressuring the team.
progress.factual: The project made steady progress through the year.
progress.general: Her reading has shown good progress.

success.simple: reaching what you set out to do
success.natural: He stayed humble after his first success.
success.positive: Success is the result of many unglamorous habits.
success.leadership: A leader shares success and carries failure alone.
success.factual: The campaign was a success, with every target met.
success.general: The function was a success thanks to the volunteers.

select.natural: He was happy to be selected for the trial.
select.positive: Select your battles carefully and finish the ones you choose.
select.leadership: The leader selected the team by skill, not by favour.
select.factual: Candidates are selected through a written exam and an interview.
select.general: Please select a colour from the list.

climb.natural: He climbed slowly and rested at every ledge.
climb.positive: Every climb is easier when the next step is clear.
climb.leadership: The leader climbed last to make sure nobody was left behind.
climb.factual: The peak was first climbed in 1953.
climb.general: The children climbed the mango tree for fruit.

task.simple: a piece of work to be done
task.natural: He finished the task before taking a break.
task.positive: A hard task done well builds quiet confidence.
task.leadership: The leader gave each person a task that matched his strength.
task.factual: The task took four hours and two people.
task.general: My only task today is to buy vegetables.

tragedy.natural: The village never forgot the tragedy of that flood.
tragedy.positive: Even after tragedy, people rebuild with courage.
tragedy.leadership: The leader reached the tragedy site before dawn.
tragedy.factual: The tragedy claimed many lives and damaged the bridge.
tragedy.general: It was a tragedy that the trip ended in rain.

weak.natural: He felt weak after the long march but kept walking.
weak.positive: A weak start can still become a strong finish.
weak.leadership: The leader protected the weakest member instead of leaving him.
weak.factual: The bridge was declared weak and closed for repairs.
weak.general: The tea is too weak for my taste.

corruption.simple: dishonest use of power for personal gain
corruption.natural: He refused to join the corruption around him.
corruption.positive: Clean systems and honest people can defeat corruption.
corruption.leadership: The leader made every payment public to stop corruption.
corruption.factual: The Lokpal investigates complaints of corruption.
corruption.general: Corruption raises the price of everything.

bluff.simple: to pretend to be strong in order to deceive
bluff.natural: He called the bluff instead of backing away.
bluff.positive: Honesty wins where bluff only delays.
bluff.leadership: The leader saw the bluff and kept the team steady.
bluff.factual: In poker, a bluff is a bet made on a weak hand.
bluff.general: He was only bluffing when he said he would leave.

borrow.simple: to take something and return it later
borrow.natural: He asked politely before borrowing the cycle.
borrow.positive: Borrowing wisely and returning on time builds trust.
borrow.leadership: The leader borrowed nothing he could not return.
borrow.factual: The bank lets students borrow for education at low interest.
borrow.general: Can I borrow your pen for a minute?

calamity.natural: The town prepared before the calamity struck.
calamity.positive: Preparedness turns a calamity into a manageable crisis.
calamity.leadership: The leader stayed calm during the calamity and gave clear orders.
calamity.factual: The calamity destroyed crops across three districts.
calamity.general: Missing the last bus was a small calamity for us.

convince.natural: He convinced his friend with facts, not force.
convince.positive: A calm explanation convinces better than a loud argument.
convince.leadership: The leader convinced the team to accept a difficult plan.
convince.factual: The evidence convinced the committee to change the rule.
convince.general: She convinced me to try the new restaurant.

duty.natural: He stayed at his post because it was his duty.
duty.positive: Duty done quietly is the strongest form of service.
duty.leadership: A leader puts duty before comfort every time.
duty.factual: Every officer takes an oath to do his duty without fear.
duty.general: It is my duty to lock the gate at night.

doubt.simple: a feeling of not being sure
doubt.natural: A small doubt made him check the figures twice.
doubt.positive: Doubt handled honestly leads to better decisions.
doubt.leadership: The leader welcomed doubt and answered every question.
doubt.factual: The report left no doubt about the cause of the failure.
doubt.general: I doubt it will rain today.

joy.natural: He felt joy when the results were announced.
joy.positive: Joy shared with others lasts longer.
joy.leadership: The leader took joy in the team's success, not his own.
joy.factual: Festivals are celebrated with music and joy across India.
joy.general: The children jumped with joy at the news.

injustice.natural: He spoke up against the injustice he saw.
injustice.positive: Courage and law together can correct injustice.
injustice.leadership: The leader refused to allow injustice in his unit.
injustice.factual: The Constitution protects citizens against injustice.
injustice.general: It was an injustice to blame the whole class.

stress.natural: He managed stress by running every morning.
stress.positive: Stress handled well sharpens your focus.
stress.leadership: The leader reduced stress by giving the team clear priorities.
stress.factual: Long hours without rest increase stress and reduce accuracy.
stress.general: Exam stress made him forget his own name.

win.natural: He wanted to win, but he played fair.
win.positive: You win twice when you win without cheating.
win.leadership: A leader wins by making the team believe in itself.
win.factual: India won the match by six wickets.
win.general: Nobody wins an argument with a stubborn person.

exploit.natural: He refused to exploit the trust of his juniors.
exploit.positive: Use your strengths to lift others, never to exploit them.
exploit.leadership: The leader made sure no worker was exploited for extra hours.
exploit.factual: The law protects children from being exploited at work.
exploit.general: They exploited the free offer and ate twice.

freedom.simple: the right to act without being controlled
freedom.natural: He valued the freedom to choose his own path.
freedom.positive: Freedom grows stronger when it is used with responsibility.
freedom.leadership: A leader gives freedom with clear limits.
freedom.factual: India became independent in 1947 after a long freedom struggle.
freedom.general: The holiday gave us the freedom to sleep late.

battlefield.simple: the place where a battle is fought
battlefield.natural: He imagined the battlefield and felt the weight of it.
battlefield.positive: Courage on a battlefield begins with discipline at home.
battlefield.leadership: The leader kept the wounded moving off the battlefield.
battlefield.factual: The battlefield was cleared and secured by nightfall.
battlefield.general: The old battlefield is now a quiet field of grass.

employment.simple: the state of having paid work
employment.natural: He searched for employment while studying at night.
employment.positive: Skill and honesty make employment easier to find.
employment.leadership: The leader trained his team so their employment was secure.
employment.factual: Employment in the services sector has grown steadily.
employment.general: The factory provides employment to three hundred people.

scheme.natural: He read the scheme carefully before applying.
scheme.positive: A good scheme reaches the people it was made for.
scheme.leadership: The leader explained the scheme in simple words to the village.
scheme.factual: The scheme gives every household a cooking gas connection.
scheme.general: Their scheme to surprise her worked perfectly.

navy.simple: the branch of the armed forces that fights at sea
navy.natural: He watched the navy ships leave the harbour.
navy.positive: The navy protects trade routes that keep the country running.
navy.leadership: The navy captain steadied the crew in rough weather.
navy.factual: The Indian Navy traces its origins to 1612.
navy.general: The navy band played at the parade.

agree.natural: He agreed only after hearing the full argument.
agree.positive: People agree faster when they feel heard.
agree.leadership: The leader got everyone to agree on one clear goal.
agree.factual: Both sides agreed to the ceasefire terms.
agree.general: I agree with your plan for the weekend.

run.natural: He ran to the gate when he heard the bell.
run.positive: A short run each morning clears the mind.
run.leadership: The leader ran beside the slowest recruit.
run.factual: He ran the distance in under four minutes.
run.general: I need to run to the shop before it closes.

life.natural: He chose to value life in every form.
life.positive: Life becomes meaningful when it serves others.
life.leadership: A leader protects life before property.
life.factual: Life expectancy in India has risen over the decades.
life.general: Life in a small town is slow and peaceful.

discipline.natural: He followed a strict discipline during training.
discipline.positive: Discipline is the bridge between a goal and its achievement.
discipline.leadership: The leader enforced discipline by example.
discipline.factual: The academy is known for its discipline and routine.
discipline.general: Discipline at home makes school easier.

courage.natural: It took courage to speak the truth in that room.
courage.positive: Courage grows every time fear is faced honestly.
courage.leadership: A leader shows courage by standing with the team in failure.
courage.factual: The soldier was awarded for courage under fire.
courage.general: She found the courage to say no.
